method_note: Concise, manually reviewed implications derived from authenticated FantasyGuru articles for the user's personal draft research. Paid article text is not reproduced. Adjustments are deliberately small and should remain subject to the application's per-signal and total context caps.

signals.summary: FantasyGuru expects Murray to be the favorite for Minnesota's Week 1 job and views him as an appealing QB2 in two-QB formats.
signals.mechanism: Kevin O'Connell's offense and Minnesota's receiving group improve Murray's passing environment, while his rushing history supports a useful fantasy floor.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Same Faces In New Places

signals.summary: FantasyGuru identifies Willis as a two-QB target because Miami committed to him and his rushing can stabilize an otherwise uncertain profile.
signals.mechanism: A starting job plus designed or improvised rushing can create QB2 value even if passing volume and supporting talent are mediocre.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Same Faces In New Places

signals.summary: New Orleans paid Etienne as a featured back, and FantasyGuru expects him to lead the backfield despite Alvin Kamara remaining on the roster.
signals.mechanism: A projected every-down role preserves rushing and receiving paths to production in a non-PPR league.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Same Faces In New Places

signals.summary: FantasyGuru projects Walker as Kansas City's every-down back after the club made a substantial multiyear investment.
signals.mechanism: A larger share of a high-value backfield can lift both touch volume and touchdown opportunity.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Same Faces In New Places

signals.summary: FantasyGuru expects Montgomery to handle early downs and meaningful red-zone work in Houston.
signals.mechanism: Short-yardage and goal-line usage can support standard-scoring RB2 value even if receiving work is limited.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Same Faces In New Places

signals.summary: FantasyGuru sees a plausible committee and red-zone role for Rodriguez behind Bhayshul Tuten.
signals.mechanism: Goal-line work creates standalone touchdown value and meaningful contingency upside at a late cost.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Same Faces In New Places

signals.summary: FantasyGuru projects Brown as New England's primary target after Stefon Diggs' departure.
signals.mechanism: A clear lead role and substantial vacated volume provide a path back to elite target totals.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Same Faces In New Places

signals.summary: FantasyGuru considers Moore a rebound target in Buffalo, where Josh Allen and frequent single-high looks improve his matchup environment.
signals.mechanism: Quarterback quality and defensive structure can restore explosive perimeter production after a down season.

signals.summary: Washington's new offensive coordinator has described an offense built around high McLaurin target volume, and the club added little veteran competition.
signals.mechanism: Formation movement and an explicit volume plan increase the probability of a target rebound.

signals.summary: FantasyGuru places Watson atop Green Bay's receiver depth chart and sees top-15 upside if he remains healthy.
signals.mechanism: A projected lead route and snap share paired with established deep efficiency creates ceiling at a price outside the top 25 receivers.

signals.summary: FantasyGuru identifies Burden as a Year 2 breakout candidate after strong per-route production and Chicago's removal of veteran target competition.
signals.mechanism: More routes and snaps can convert an already strong target rate and yards-per-route profile into dependable volume.

signals.summary: FantasyGuru views Denver's high-volume passing environment and Bo Nix pairing as a material upgrade for Waddle.
signals.mechanism: A larger passing-volume base can offset added target competition and restore weekly ceiling.

signals.summary: Arizona's new staff plans to move Harrison among the slot, X, and Z alignments after an injury-affected 2025.
signals.mechanism: More varied deployment can create easier touches and improve consistency for a receiver previously used too statically.

signals.summary: FantasyGuru notes Washington led Jacksonville in several per-route measures over its final eight games and projects him ahead of Travis Hunter entering 2026.
signals.mechanism: A growing role in a historically productive slot assignment creates a plausible low-cost breakout path.

signals.summary: FantasyGuru expects Philadelphia's rookie to benefit from vacated targets and a new coordinator with a crossing-route-oriented coaching background.
signals.mechanism: Immediate slot access plus a scheme suited to yards after the catch creates late-round upside.

signals.summary: FantasyGuru highlights Concepcion's separation and open-field profile plus limited target competition in Cleveland.
signals.mechanism: A versatile rookie with a credible route to early targets offers late-round ceiling, though quarterback play limits confidence.

signals.summary: FantasyGuru lists Metcalf as a fade because Pittsburgh's quick-pass design and added receiver competition may squeeze his targets.
signals.mechanism: A low-depth passing approach is a poor fit for a receiver dependent on deep plays and touchdowns.

signals.summary: FantasyGuru sees Likely as a breakout candidate after reuniting with John Harbaugh on a meaningful contract in New York.
signals.mechanism: Prior production without Mark Andrews and a credible path to being the Giants' second target support a larger receiving role.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Same Faces In New Places

signals.summary: FantasyGuru still prefers Gadsden atop the Chargers' tight-end room but notes added competition and Mike McDaniel's historically low 12-personnel use.
signals.mechanism: Fewer two-tight-end packages and more competition reduce route certainty, limiting the breakout case.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Same Faces In New Places

signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Green Bay's line poorly outside of right tackle Zach Tom and flags major interior concerns.
signals.mechanism: Weak interior blocking can reduce rushing efficiency and increase pressure on Jordan Love.

signals.summary: FantasyGuru identifies Denver as a top line returning all five starters after ranking first in pass blocking in 2025.
signals.mechanism: Continuity and strong protection improve the stability of both passing and rushing production.

signals.summary: FantasyGuru describes Chicago's line as one of the league's best after top-five pass- and run-blocking results in 2025.
signals.mechanism: Strong blocking raises the floor for Caleb Williams and the running game, though the center transition bears watching.

signals.summary: Cleveland is rebuilding a line that ranked last in pass blocking and near the bottom in run blocking in 2025.
signals.mechanism: Extensive turnover creates early cohesion risk even though the new starters could eventually improve the unit.

signals.summary: As of August 16, Pierce was still not practicing following offseason ankle surgery, putting his Week 1 readiness in doubt.
signals.mechanism: Missed practice time and a possible delayed start reduce near-term availability and role certainty.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Fantasy Billboard: 105 Draft Board Observations

signals.summary: FantasyGuru's August 16 update reports Hubbard as week-to-week with a hamstring injury, citing head coach Dave Canales.
signals.mechanism: A soft-tissue injury close to the season creates availability and workload risk.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Fantasy Billboard: 105 Draft Board Observations

signals.summary: FantasyGuru reports Brooks healthy and drawing positive camp attention while Hubbard is dealing with a hamstring injury.
signals.mechanism: Improved health plus a temporary opening ahead of him increases contingency value, but does not establish a starting role.
signals.source_name: FantasyGuru - Fantasy Billboard: 105 Draft Board Observations
